key_insight: The exact sampling overhead for implementing collective diagonal quadratic phases is determined by the continued-fraction structure of \u03b3/\u03c0, with rational angles giving finite exact costs and badly approximable angles forcing linear growth in system size.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum algorithm designers a precise cost rule for Kerr-like, spin-squeezing, and constrained-optimization phase layers, helping choose angles and decompositions with provable sampling overhead.
method: Characterize the target gate e^{-i\u03b3K^2} as an LCU over single-qubit rotation layers.
Derive exact minimal overheads using number-theoretic properties of \u03b3/\u03c0, including rational and badly approximable cases.
Prove optimality via lower bounds, including a certificate-lifting argument for non-symmetric binary-weighted observables.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact threshold results, tight two-sided formulas near low-denominator rationals, and lower/upper bounds matching known Fourier-based and Kerr-optimal decompositions.
watch_item: The strongest exact optimality claims depend on symmetry and on the angle class; for non-symmetric observables or irrational angles, overhead can become much larger and implementation may be impractical.
paper_title: The exact LCU sampling overhead of collective diagonal unitaries: resonances and a continued-fraction dichotomy
